questions.question: Wheels with welding repairs are:

options.text: Safe if a professional did the repairs.
Safe if the repair looks solid.

questions.explanation: Welded wheels or rims are not safe. Replace them before driving.

questions.question: To control surge when stopping, you should not:

options.text: Keep steady pressure on the brakes.

questions.explanation: To prevent surge in a tank vehicle, keep steady brake pressure and do not release the brakes too early. Brake well in advance and leave more space between vehicles.

questions.question: When driving a triple combination, keep the rear shut-off valves of the middle trailer in their:
questions.explanation: Close the shut-off valves at the rear of the last trailer. Keep all other shut-off valves open.

questions.question: When checking your tires, you do not want to find:

options.text: Tire tread that is 4/32 of an inch deep.
Valve stems that are not damaged.

questions.explanation: Front tires need at least 4/32 inch of tread depth. Other tires need at least 2/32 inch. Valve stems must not be cut or cracked. All tires must be the same size.

questions.question: When should you turn off a retarder for safety?

options.text: When you are carrying a heavy load.

questions.explanation: Retarders help slow your vehicle. But they can cause wheels to skid on wet, snowy, or icy roads. Turn them off in these conditions.

questions.question: What is the Johnson bar?

options.text: A hand valve that controls the trailer brakes.
A valve that shows the fuel level.
A valve that limits cargo amount.

questions.correctAnswerText: A hand valve that controls the trailer brakes.
questions.explanation: The Johnson bar (also called the trolley valve) is a hand valve for the trailer brakes. Use it only to test the brakes. Using it while moving can cause a skid.

questions.question: Which is not a recommended way to spot trouble?

options.text: Checking critical items only at the start and end of a trip.

questions.correctAnswerText: Checking critical items only at the start and end of a trip.
questions.explanation: Check your vehicle often during a trip, not just at the beginning and end. Watch your gauges, mirrors, tires, cargo, and lights. Use all your senses to spot problems early.

questions.question: A Class 1 hazardous material is:
questions.explanation: Class 1 hazardous materials include explosives like ammunition, dynamite, and fireworks.

questions.question: When should mirrors be adjusted?
questions.explanation: Adjust mirrors before you start driving. If you have a trailer, it must be straight for accurate mirror adjustment.

questions.question: An empty truck:

options.text: Stops faster than a full truck.
Takes longer to stop than a full truck.
Takes the same distance to stop as a full truck.

questions.correctAnswerText: Takes longer to stop than a full truck.
questions.explanation: Empty trucks need longer stopping distances than full trucks because they have less traction.

questions.question: How do you prevent a trailer from rolling over while turning?
questions.explanation: Trailers roll over when you turn too fast. Always slow down before entering turns and curves, especially when pulling a trailer.

questions.question: Where must placards be placed on a vehicle carrying hazardous cargo?

options.text: On the front, rear, and sides.

questions.correctAnswerText: On the front, rear, and sides.
questions.explanation: Placards must be on the front, rear, and both sides of the vehicle so they can be seen from any direction.

questions.question: When coupling a second trailer, how should you secure it?

options.text: Place it at the base of a hill.

questions.explanation: Use wheel chocks to secure the trailer while coupling if you are unsure about the trailer's brakes.

questions.question: When should you do an after-trip inspection?
questions.explanation: Complete an after-trip inspection at the end of each trip, day, or shift. Fill out a vehicle inspection report if required.

questions.question: How can you stay alert while driving?

options.text: Keep the cab cool by using air conditioning or opening a window.
Eat a lot of heavy food.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep the cab cool by using air conditioning or opening a window.
questions.explanation: To avoid fatigue, keep the cab cool. Also avoid heavy foods and take rest breaks every two hours or 100 miles.

questions.question: What should you do if you doubt your vehicle fits under a bridge or sign?
questions.explanation: Slow down if you are not sure your vehicle will fit. Take a different route if possible.

questions.question: If a jackknife starts, what should you never do?
questions.explanation: If the trailer starts to jackknife, release the brakes and let the trailer wheels regain grip. Do not use the trailer hand brake, as it will make the skid worse.

questions.question: What should you use to put out an electrical fire?
questions.explanation: B:C fire extinguishers work on electrical fires and burning liquids. Never use water on an electrical fire.

questions.question: When should you slow down and be extra careful?
questions.explanation: Slow down and be careful in work zones, where pavement drops off sharply, when objects are on the road, and on freeway ramps.

questions.question: When stopping a manual transmission vehicle, what should you do?

options.text: Push the clutch in when the engine is near idle.
Push the clutch out when the engine is near idle.
Shift into neutral when the engine is near idle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Push the clutch in when the engine is near idle.
questions.explanation: Apply steady pressure to the brake and stop smoothly. With a manual transmission, push the clutch in when the engine is near idle.
